name: Quan Cong Temple
kicker: Temple to Quan Cong on Trần Phú
summary: The temple at 24 Trần Phú built for Quan Công in the mid-17th century. In the main hall he sits in a dragon robe beside two attendants and two life-size horses, one white and one red. A short stop on the Trần Phú walk; on the 16th of the first lunar month it fills with worshippers.
fee: 20,000 VND from 10 Aug 2026, or a combination ticket
heroCaption: The temple front on Trần Phú, roof and doors in one frame

notice.title: It is a temple to Quan Cong, not a Buddhist pagoda
notice.body: The name says chùa, but this is a hall for Quan Công, built about 1653. Dress for a working temple.

body: Walk in from 24 Trần Phú. Four buildings stand in a chữ khẩu plan: a front court, two side houses, and a main hall, under a tube-tile roof carved with dragons. The main hall holds Quan Vân Trường in a dragon robe, the attendant Châu Thương, the adopted son Quan Bình, and two horses the size of real horses, a white one and a red hare. The hall also keeps poems written in 1775 by Xuân Quận Công Nguyễn Nghiễm, the father of Nguyễn Du, with replies by Uông Sĩ Cư and Nguyễn Lệnh Tân.

The hall dates to about 1653, built by Hoa merchants settled in the port together with Minh Hương and Vietnamese neighbours. It became a national historic relic on 29 November 1991. On the combination ticket it is the other landmark choice beside the Japanese bridge.
Come in the morning, unless your date is the 16th of the first lunar month, when the crowd comes for Nguyên tiêu. In a flood week Trần Phú can be under water.

figures.caption: The statue in the main hall
figures.alt: A seated statue in a blue robe inside Quan Cong Temple in Hoi An, with an incense burner and red banners

gettingThere: The hall is at 24 Trần Phú, in the old town. Walk from the lanes off the core.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk along Trần Phú to number 24.

admissionNote: No separate price for this building. From 10 Aug 2026: 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). Heritage centre notices of 26 Jan and 16 Mar 2026: 80,000 VND (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) or 120,000 VND (adds a museum and three other works), usable through a stay of up to three days. A May 2026 article counts those as four and six works. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale. During the 2026 Nguyên tiêu festival the centre did not sell a ticket for this hall.
